title: A budget ceiling on a pay-per-token account counts what that account pays, so Bedrock's regional premium counts
description: The router keeps a step under the project's `budgetCeiling` by comparing it with each profile's `costPerTaskUsd` (`withinCeiling` in apps/daemon/src/routing/router.ts). That cost is Artificial Analysis's cost per task, measured at the maker's list price. The account's own price is already in the catalogue (`priceOf` in apps/daemon/src/catalogue/account-offer.ts): a subscription account pays nothing per token, so its price is null; an API key or a gateway pays the maker's list price; a Bedrock account pays the price of its own copy of the model, about 10% more in a regional profile. So on Bedrock a ceiling under-counts what a task costs. The builder chose this: on an account that pays per token, scale the cost per task by the account's output price divided by the maker's output price before comparing it with the ceiling. A subscription keeps the maker's figure, because there a ceiling measures how heavy a model is, not dollars.
acceptanceCriteria: On a Bedrock account whose copy of a model costs 10% more than the maker's, a step whose maker-priced cost per task is just under the project's ceiling is over the ceiling, and the step's routing reason says so
On an API-key account, which pays the maker's price, the same step is routed exactly as today
On a Claude subscription or ChatGPT sign-in account, ceilings route exactly as today
Where the routing reason names a cost against the ceiling, the cost it names is the one the ceiling was compared with
